findings.title: Callable reviewed-return path admits PublicToolLoan-backed requests
findings.trigger: An active staff actor with RETURN_REQUEST for the tenant posts a quantity-mode direct or public loan's HardwareRequest id to admin/requests/<pk>/return with valid return evidence, a remark and resolutions. No container code is needed because these loan requests do not populate HardwareRequest.assigned_box.
findings.reason: The API's _scoped_action_request filters only action/tenant, and _require_returnable checks only issued/partially_returned status. return_items changes item quantities and HardwareRequest state but never changes the related PublicToolLoan. The queue exclusion does not protect the callable endpoint. This bypasses the loan-specific return QR/owner/source handling and leaves active loan/QR/container records outstanding.
findings.consequence: A fully resolved request can coexist with a checked_out loan. For a public quantity loan, resolving one unit as damaged/missing through this endpoint and later using the normal public return also reaches _return_request_items, which subtracts only returned_quantity. With sufficient product issued stock on other loans, it can credit an already damaged/missing unit back to available and debit another loan's issued bucket.
findings.validation_basis: Direct source trace; no runtime reproduction or tests performed.

findings.title: Scanning a box can issue individual assets without their own QR scans
findings.trigger: A box contains an AVAILABLE individual asset whose product has available stock. For the public path, the asset and product have the public checkout flags enabled and the product itself need not be assigned to that box. Submit only the box QR with valid issue evidence through public checkout or staff direct handout.
findings.reason: _checkout_box selects assets using box membership and eligibility flags, delegates their quantities and bulk-updates their statuses to ISSUED. It neither resolves nor requires each asset's QR payload. The callers record scan events only for supplied QRs, so only the box scan is recorded. Supplying the box and contained asset QRs together is explicitly rejected by _reject_overlapping_checkout_targets.
findings.consequence: Individually tracked tools can leave custody without the per-unit QR proof required by AGENTS.md and docs/INVARIANTS.md:417-421, including tools with no active asset QR.
findings.validation_basis: Direct source trace with model fields checked; no runtime reproduction or tests performed.

findings.title: Selected-container direct issue reverses public checkout's QR/box lock order
findings.trigger: Concurrent valid public checkout and staff direct handout target the same free box QR. The direct request supplies both container_id=B and qr_payloads containing B's box QR; the two operations use different evidence rows.
findings.reason: The direct transaction locks Box B at lines 80-82 before attempting its QR lock at line 129. Public checkout locks that QrCode at self_checkout_workflow.py:78 before _checkout_box attempts Box B at self_checkout_helpers.py:80. If each transaction acquires its first row before the other, direct waits for the QR while public waits for the box. Direct issue does not share public checkout's initial tenant-row serialization.
findings.consequence: The wait cycle can cause PostgreSQL to abort one handout transaction for deadlock. The workflow exception mapping inspected does not translate database deadlock OperationalError into a domain conflict.
findings.validation_basis: Concrete source-level lock acquisition cycle; no concurrent runtime reproduction performed.
